intent.description: What the change does, in a few words the author reads in the app, such as "Bars rise one by one".

operations.description: Batch compatible edits as one Undo step, or send one standalone operation. Every number keeps the millionth.

revision.description: From presentations.get or slides.get; stale when a slide it changes has changed, or anything, for a deck-wide change.

AgentAnimationMoment.description: The moment in a slide's motion an edit lands at, as the Animate tab's playhead sets it for the Inspector and the keyframe buttons: Start (`stepId` null), or `time` in a step.

content.description: Initial text and file values keyed by inherited object id.

controls.description: A composition's controls; only with `role: composition`.

name.description: A composition's name; only with `role: composition`.

role.description: Makes the slide a composition, a reusable scene other slides place; `size`, `controls` and `name` belong to it alone.

size.description: A composition's own size; only with `role: composition`.

slideId.description: Minted when omitted; the batch may place slides against it, and later proposals change its objects.

afterStepId.description: Insert after this step; null means first, omitted means last.

stepIds.description: The new steps' ids, one per step, so a later `updateStep` or `tween` of the same batch, or the next proposal, addresses them without reading them back; minted when omitted.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

exponential-scale.description: Whether the move to this keyframe scales at an even rate, as After Effects' Exponential Scale does.

end.description: Original endpoint in step seconds; must be at or after time and does not extend the step.

value.description: Original interpolation endpoint, admitted against the same target as value.

incoming.description: Preserve an interpolation prefix before this keyframe; at time, value applies immediately.

interpolation.description: Interpolation into this keyframe, from the preceding keyframe or the step's start.

oscillate.description: A swing added from this keyframe on, its wave named as the file names it.

path.description: On a path pair's x keyframe, `frame.x` or `translation.x`: the move into it, with the pair's y keyframe there, bends along this path.

start.description: When the move into this keyframe begins, in step seconds; until then the value before it holds. Absent, at the keyframe before.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

value.description: Null clears an optional property; its current text-style/default then applies.

keyframes.description: Shared keyframe/cue ID namespace. An existing ID replaces the whole event; outer null deletes it.

loop-from.description: Step seconds where the loop while waiting begins; null removes the loop.

loops.description: Each named curve's loop whole, its word and the keyframe it loops from; null takes it off. No keyframe's edit changes it.

repeat.description: Play the step this many times; null plays once.

start.description: Play with the step before it or after it ends, within its click; null waits for a click.

AgentEnterEffect.description: The Animate tab's builds, as core names them.

rotation.description: Authored degrees. Animation keyframes allow explicit turns.

AgentRevision.description: An opaque revision from presentations.get, slides.get or an accept, naming the presentation as you last saw it; the one value that guards a change.

AgentSpaceTransform.description: A 3D object's move: any parts of its position, its whole rotation in its rotation mode and any parts of a model's or a light's scale. The parts it leaves out stay as they are.

anyOf.description: The Animate tab's and the timeline's timing edits, each as the app makes it.

AgentStepEditSource.description: A timing edit in the file's words: `loop-keyframe` and a keyframe's `exponential-scale`, and a swing's `wave-shape`.

AgentTransformFrame.description: The frame a transform gives an object, where it is drawn: every side, but a table's height only where the edit sizes the table. A text box that grows to its words may leave its height out, as a height sizes nothing there; a width its words give it sizes nothing either.

exponential-scale.description: On a `scale` or `crop.scale` change: reach `to` at one rate of zoom, as a camera push does; absent, it changes evenly.

AgentTweenChangeSource.description: A tween's change in the file's words.

at.description: Last checkpoint or deletion position; a live target takes precedence.

The scene's `animationValueSchemas` gives the range of each channel the slide's objects offer, by kind of object. Core refuses a value outside its channel's range and names both.

PresentationDrawnTextFrame.description: A text box's frame where it is drawn, as an insert or a paste gives it. One that grows to its words (auto-size height or both, on no path) is as tall as they are: a height given sizes nothing. One whose words give it its width (auto-size width or both, on no path, in one column) is as wide as they are: the width given sizes nothing, and the box grows from the point its alignment holds on the frame given.

PresentationPropertyChangeSource.description: One of the presentation's own properties and its value, as the file keys and spells it; null takes it away.

PresentationReplicaArrangement.description: A replica's copies in a grid a gap apart, or a ring a radius from the selection's center, as groups and repeaters.

PresentationRotation3d.description: How a 3D object turns, in degrees about the 3D space's axes (x right, y up, z toward the viewer), in Cinema 4D's HPB order: heading about y, then pitch about its own x, then bank about its own z, three.js's YXZ Euler. A positive z turns it counterclockwise on the slide, a positive x tilts its top toward the viewer and a positive y brings its left side forward. With the rotation mode "quaternion" it is a quaternion instead, `w` and `x`, `y`, `z` in the same axes, which a key interpolates part by part and the turn reads normalized. A model's Blender quaternion (w, x, y, z), exported to glTF with +Y up, is (w, x, z, −y) here.

PresentationStepCueSource.description: What a cue starts, as the file spells it: its `type`, and a clip's `media-trim`, `blend-in` and `clip-scale`.

duration.description: Minimum seconds for this step; left out or 0, it lasts as long as what it holds.

repeat.description: Play the step this many times before it completes; omitted plays once.

start.description: Plays without a click of its own: with the step before it, or after that step ends, as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous do. Its times then count from that start. On the first step it plays after the transition. Omitted, the step waits for a click.

PresentationStepInputSource.description: A step as a proposal spells it; its curves may be left out, as a step that only waits or cues has none.

PresentationTableFrame.description: A table's frame as the files hold it: its height is its rows', and never stored.
